gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per amp-hour or per watt-hour at today's maker-store prices. On 2026-11-10 the same 100Ah of 12V LiFePO4 costs $2.34/Ah from Redodo (trolling-motor model), $3.03/Ah from LiTime (TM Bluetooth) and $3.19/Ah from Renogy (trolling-motor Bluetooth), against $6.49/Ah for Ionic and $7.99/Ah for Battle Born. That is a 2.1–3.4× premium for the 'premium' picks.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Ionic trolling-motor page, which gives $649, 29 lb and 1,280 Wh for its 12V 100Ah but no per-Wh or per-lb figure and no cross-brand comparison. I also compared against ChatGPT's own cards ($355.99 LiTime, $849 Battle Born, $335.34 Renogy, $795 Dakota), which quote prices that have since moved and never normalise them. I could not read the full text of the cited Wired2Fish guide (HTTP 403 to WebFetch; curl was not approved) or of solargenadvisor.com (TLS error), so I cannot rule out that one of them prints a $/Wh figure. That uncertainty is why I scored this 2 and not 3.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's 'best value' pick (LiTime 12V 100Ah TM Bluetooth, now $302.59, not the $355.99 on its card) and puts a number on the premium tier. Battle Born ($799) and Ionic ($649) cost 2.6× and 2.1× as much per Ah for the same 100Ah. For the energy, Ionic's 44.1 Wh/lb is roughly matched or beaten by budget packs: Redodo 12V 50Ah 56.8 Wh/lb, Redodo Ultra-Mini 12V 100Ah 64.6 Wh/lb. Redodo's trolling-motor 100Ah ($233.99, on Dealectric's own list) undercuts every card ChatGPT showed. Whether the premium buys anything (warranty: Battle Born 10 years; cells, support) is for another angle; the arithmetic alone favours LiTime or Redodo.
